A CATEGORY OF ITS OWN

The origin. Outside rarity.

unsig #00000 has no properties and is the collection's special algorithm-bearing outlier. It is excluded from all rarity calculations.

Explore any ID from 00001 to 31118 to compare rarity facets.

UNDER THE SURFACE

Count the uncommon.

Rarity starts with a simple idea: the fewer members a group has, the rarer it is. Each facet shows how many eligible unsigs share that characteristic.

Check more than one facet and Total rarity measures the actual combination. It counts the unsigs matching all your selections, then displays the percentage of the collection that does not match.

RARITY %100 × (1 − matches / 31,118)

For example, 3 matches gives 99.9904%. This is inverse frequency, not a percentile rank. Ties are expected. No single “most rare” item is required.

Data, geometry decisions & preview notes +

Geometry code is the primary classification. Named forms are not used in scoring. All 84 members of 3F-075 stay in one group, even when their detailed boundary patterns differ.

Five project assignments differ from the published reference: #19656, #19686 and #21565 use 3F-108; #29883 and #30287 use 3F-094. These decisions are supported by original-page review and structural comparison. Reference codes are preserved and shown on affected results; these are project decisions, not official taxonomy revisions.

Color clusters use published unsig.info memberships ↗. Geometry definitions and memberships were checked against unsig.info's geometry catalog ↗. Rarity is calculated from this site's reviewed snapshot, not marketplace prices or generation probabilities.

Previews adapt the creator's rendering notebook ↗, with explicit modular arithmetic. They are parameter reconstructions, not certified archival image copies. See renderer license.

Dataset snapshot: October 23, 2026 · 31,118 eligible items · 172 geometry codes · 132 color clusters. #00000 is excluded throughout.
